column1: # Core options worth changing ON A PLAYSTATION 4, per core. ps4/make-site.py reads this and shows
# it on cores.prx0.com under "Recommended settings"; nothing else does.
# ⚠ ONLY WHAT THIS PORT CHANGES OR WHAT WAS MEASURED HERE. A core's own defaults are chosen for a
# desktop GPU and a desktop CPU, and some of them are wrong on this console for reasons that are
# ours: Trident's ubershader default is the case that started this file - this port compiles the
# specialised shaders in the background instead, which only pays off with ubershaders off. General
# advice that applies on every platform belongs in the core's own documentation, not here.
# Columns, tab-separated (runs of tabs are fine):
#   core       the index name, without _libretro (the same key as core-tested.tsv)
#   key        the option's key in the core's .opt file, so the row can be checked against the
#              core's source; "-" for a RetroArch setting rather than a core option
#   label      what the user sees: the label in Quick Menu -> Options, or the RetroArch menu path
#   value      what to set it to, as the menu shows it - RetroArch shows enabled/disabled as ON/OFF
#   why        one short public sentence
#   evidence   where it was measured or decided. HANDOFF.md is
#              ps4-mesa-docs/docs/retroarch/HANDOFF.md. Not shown on the page.
trident
column5: The PS4 build draws with the ubershader only while the faster shader compiles in the background; left on, every frame takes the slow path. Off by default from 2026-09-15; an options file saved earlier may still say ON.
column6: HANDOFF.md, "shader-compile stutter", table 3: ubershader ON ~45 ms frames, async 51 frames >40 ms on the same OoT3D route
